title: Asthma, mountain air and smoky rooms
summary: The mountain air relieved his childhood asthma, which has recently returned; he blames sinus, allergies and years in smoky clubs.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Yes. Could find them. And so, we worked out there in the mountains and I was -- I enjoyed working out in the mountains because I had always had asthma, you know, as a kid coming up, and I didn't realize it. While out in those mountains -- must have cured me, and I had no idea that was what was happening, but --
Good air. And out in those mountains and everything and so I really enjoyed it. But --
Did it cure the asthma though permanently or what?
Not permanently, because it's back now. Now I wheeze. I've been wheezing now for about the last year and a half.
What do you think has caused that to come back then?
Well, that -- well, my sinus. See, my sinus and then the sinus can hit you from so many directions
and the sinus hit me from so many different directions plus allergies, you know, and that's --
That is bad. There's no question about it.
Also, I mean, playing in a smoky place.
That's true. And then when you stop and think about it, you've been playing a lot of years of your life in these places where there's smoke and you know what I mean?

And I'm sure that's what brought it back, you know what I mean, which today, now I wheeze and then -- so I take these pills for congestion and so forth like that. Well, it's just a matter -- for that night, okay, maybe the next two nights, you might not, but the next thing you know, you're wheezing right back again, you know?
Yeah, that's too bad because, you know, that's a very bad thing that gets hold of you.
